one_liner: Zig io_uring HTTP/1.1 benchmark server and young library; 1.35x nginx's HttpArena baseline rate, ties libreactorng.
what_it_does: Two codebases share the name. The measured one is MDA2AV/HttpArena frameworks/zeemo: a ~370 KB static musl binary that answers only /baseline11 (sum of query values plus POST body), /pipeline and /json/{count} through a hard-coded path switch. The repo at repo_url is a library refactor of that server (May 18-20, 2026) with a router (server.get), middleware chain, typed JSON body parsing, static files, RFC 7807 errors and OpenSSL TLS. Handlers are synchronous fn(req, res) functions, and the library has its own API, not a drop-in for nginx or any C server API.
how_it_is_fast: It forks one shared-nothing worker process per CPU allowed by the cgroup and pins each one with sched_setaffinity. Each worker has its own SO_REUSEPORT listener and a 4096-entry io_uring ring with multishot accept. A recv is posted straight into the connection's 2 KiB parser buffer. drainAndSend parses every complete pipelined request in that buffer and writes the responses back to back into a 4 KiB per-connection buffer, then sends them with one send SQE. Responses carry only a status line plus Content-Type and Content-Length (66 bytes for /pipeline), with no Date or Server header. HttpArena's description also claims 'registered provided-buffer rings', but neither main.zig nor the library's server.zig sets up a buffer ring, registered buffers or multishot recv.
when_to_use: As a 1,223-line reference (four files, tests included) for a fork-per-CPU io_uring HTTP/1.1 loop in Zig 0.16: multishot accept, an fd-indexed slot table and pipelined response batching.
As a starting design for small fixed responses on Linux with many keep-alive connections, where per-response header bytes dominate.
To study pipelined-response batching: 49.9M req/s at 16-deep pipelining on 64 hardware threads, though zix's 58.8M on the same profile is higher.
For trying the library API on a Linux kernel 5.19 or later. The repo has no license, so you can read it but not ship it.
when_not_to_use: In any product or shipped code: the repo has no LICENSE, so it is not legally reusable.
When you need HTTP/2, HTTP/3, non-Linux platforms or async handlers. Handlers are synchronous, so one blocking handler stalls that CPU's whole worker.

When raw throughput is the only reason: on baseline-4096 it is level with libreactorng (+1%) and slightly behind zix (Zig, 4,442,329 req/s). It trails libioma, libreactorng, zix and nginx on limited-conn-4096, and zix beats it on pipelining.

When an idle server's CPU cost matters: at the fixed 10k req/s latency profile it spends 30.5 us of CPU per request, against 25.2 for libreactorng, 27.5 for libioma and 27.3 for zix (from HttpArena cpu_per_req_us).

When a client may send large requests: the measured engine closes the connection when headers exceed 2 KiB or a body exceeds 512 B, and closes any accepted fd numbered 4096 or higher in a worker. The library makes these buffer sizes configurable.

integration.dependencies: Library: libc plus system OpenSSL (libssl and libcrypto, linked unconditionally because src/tls.zig references the symbols). The measured HttpArena engine depends only on Zig std.
integration.platforms: Linux only (io_uring; docs say kernel 5.19 or later); x86-64 and aarch64 builds in the Dockerfile
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded event loop per forked worker process. Nothing is shared at runtime; state is seeded before fork and shared copy-on-write.

gotchas: Measured code differs from the repo: the HttpArena numbers come from the raw-socket engine in MDA2AV/HttpArena frameworks/zeemo, last changed by its author 2026-05-18. The library's own HttpArena entry (zeemo-tuned, PR #739) has no results file (site/data/results/zeemo-tuned.json returns 404), so the library API has no published numbers.

Description flaw: meta.json and the catalogue's why_faster credit 'registered provided-buffer rings', but neither main.zig nor the library's server.zig sets up a buffer ring, registered buffers or multishot recv. The phrase appears to be copied from libioma's and libreactorng's descriptions. The library README's 'multishot accept and recv' is also only half true: accept is multishot, recv is single-shot.

Header-volume advantage: responses omit Date and Server. gcannon's bandwidth column uses binary units (3.06 GB/s / 49,860,224 req/s = 65.9 B, exactly the 66-byte /pipeline response), so per-response sizes at baseline-4096 are about 66 B for zeemo, 114 B for libreactorng and 142 B for nginx. These are about 5% above the verifier's decimal-unit figures, with the same ratios (derived from page data).

The README's '#1 on json-4096' refers to a profile HttpArena removed on 2026-08-29 (#1375). That JSON handler copied item objects pre-rendered at startup (dataset.zig) and computed only the total per request. At baseline-4096 zeemo also used more CPU than libreactorng (6410.6% vs 6168.4%), so per CPU-second libreactorng served about 3% more requests (derived from page data).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely. zix (Zig) is faster on baseline-4096, pipelined-4096 and limited-conn-4096 and adds TLS and database routes, while libxev and the C# minima-sync entry land within 1% on baseline. Pick zeemo only to read a minimal, dependency-free single-binary io_uring loop, and only as reference, since it has no license.
verified_claims_summary: HttpArena, Threadripper PRO 3995WX with the server pinned to 32 cores / 64 threads and gcannon on the other half over loopback, best of three 5 s runs. At 4096 keep-alive connections zeemo (Zig 0.16 ReleaseFast, baseline x86-64 target) served 4,422,489 req/s vs nginx with a custom C module at -O3 -march=native 3,284,513 (1.35x), libreactorng 4,377,377 (1.01x, a tie) and Drogon 2,022,710. At 16-deep pipelining it served 49.9M vs libreactorng 43.4M. With connections closed every 10 requests it was 0.99x nginx.
status_note: A three-day project (20 commits, May 18-20, 2026), 4 stars, no open issues and no license file, so reference-only. The measured engine in the HttpArena repo has had only maintainer profile edits since May 18, 2026.
